title: Ang 1251–1253: Sarang's Bhagats
tomorrow: the sky over the truck yard goes dark. which raga was made for this?

segments.voice: Yesterday, ang 1245: the ballad ended on hands, not titles. Work for what you eat, and give some from your own hand. Raga Sarang has a few pages left.

Simran's college housing form is down to its last question: would you prefer a roommate who shares your religious practices? Yes, no, no preference. Her cursor hovers. Bebe would say yes before the question finished. Maya would laugh at her for even pausing. And the page Simran read last night, at the very end of raga Sarang, has a line that seems to settle it. Or does it?
screen: `ONE QUESTION LEFT ON THE FORM.` → `BEBE: YES. MAYA: LAUGHS.` → `A LINE THAT SEEMS TO SETTLE IT.`

segments.voice: After the ballad, raga Sarang closes with the bhagats, on ang 1251 to 1253: Kabir, Namdev, Parmanand and Surdas. They're devotees from outside the line of Gurus, and their hymns sit in the Granth beside the Gurus' own. The last of them, Surdas, gives the line. In paraphrase: leave, O mind, the company of those turned away from God. Sikh readers hear it two ways. The first reading takes it plainly. Company shapes a mind. The Granth praises the sangat, the company of seekers, because the room you sit in becomes you. On this reading, wanting a roommate who keeps the same early prayers isn't narrow. It's care for what you're becoming. The second reading asks what turned away means. It names a direction, not a label. These very pages gather voices from different births and backgrounds, and the Sikh prayer, Ardas, ends by asking for sarbat da bhala, the good of all. So the question is what a person turns you toward, not what box they tick. A kind roommate from any background might turn you toward God; a careless one from your own might not. Here's something to tell a friend tonight: the four voices that close raga Sarang are bhagats, not Gurus, and the Gurus kept their songs. Simran ticks no preference. Then yes. Then no preference again. The form saves whatever she leaves there. The question stays open.
screen: `FOUR BHAGATS CLOSE RAGA SARANG.` · `SURDAS: LEAVE THE TURNED-AWAY.` · `ONE READING: COMPANY SHAPES YOU.` · `THE OTHER: A DIRECTION, NOT A LABEL.` · then, large: `FOUR BHAGATS.`

segments.voice: If you have paper nearby, write down the names of two people you spend the most time with this month. Next to each, write one word for what they turn you toward. Then put the pen down and sit with the list for the rest of the time, breathing easily, judging no one, yourself included.
Ang 1251. Where the bhagats close raga Sarang: Kabir, Namdev, Parmanand and Surdas, and a line about the company you keep.
Hold onto this: four bhagats, and one question, what your company turns you toward. Until tomorrow.
